> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #276 addresses issue #275, where `/implement` requests made from a PR could ask for stacked follow-up work but the dispatched implementation PR still targeted `main`.
- The PR adds deterministic base derivation so explicit stacked/follow-up implement requests on PR targets pass `base_pr=<source PR>` into the existing implementation workflow.
- It also forwards target metadata through router and approval paths, updates docs, and adds focused regression tests for the happy path.
- The overall design reuses the existing `base_pr` resolution path, which is the right integration point.

## Review
The core approach is sound, but two false-positive paths remain. No material reviewer disagreement: the rubrics review passed, while the code reviews flagged concrete edge cases in the new inference behavior.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Over-broad stacked intent detection | WARNING | The bare `\bstacked\b` regex treats ordinary feature text like “stacked layout” as stacked-PR intent. On PR targets, that can silently retarget an implement run to the source PR. |
| Base inference also runs on label target context | WARNING | For `agent/implement` label triggers on PRs, `REQUEST_TEXT` can be the PR title/body rather than an explicit command. Target prose mentioning “follow-up PR” or “stacked PR” can accidentally derive `base_pr`. |

## Progress
- PR #276 implements the intended happy path for issue #275 by deriving `base_pr` for explicit stacked/follow-up PR requests.
- Rubrics review passed with no rubric-specific follow-up.
- Reviewer verification reported `npm run build`, targeted node tests, and `git diff --check` passing.
- Posted inline comments for both unresolved warnings: `.agent/src/implementation-base-hint.ts:16` and `.agent/src/cli/dispatch-agent-implement.ts:26`.
- No existing inline comments or review threads were present before those comments.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Over-broad stacked intent detection</summary>

**Cause:** [`implementation-base-hint.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/5d4cc8395c3122390f1d7e80a7550e0f719c15e2/.agent/src/implementation-base-hint.ts#L16) includes `/\bstacked\b/i`, so any standalone “stacked” matches even without PR/base context.

**Candidate solutions:** Require explicit PR/base wording, such as `stacked PR`, `stacked pull request`, `stack on this`, or fold `stacked` into the more contextual pattern. Add negative tests for ordinary uses like “stacked layout” or “stacked cache”.

**Comments:** This is actionable because the helper currently derives `base_pr` whenever the target is a PR and the pattern matches.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Base inference also runs on label target context</summary>

**Cause:** [`dispatch-agent-implement.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/5d4cc8395c3122390f1d7e80a7550e0f719c15e2/.agent/src/cli/dispatch-agent-implement.ts#L26) runs the detector on generic `REQUEST_TEXT`. For label-triggered PR events, context extraction can populate that body from the target PR title/body, not a slash-command request.

**Candidate solutions:** Pass structured trigger/source context into the dispatch CLI and only infer a stacked base for explicit command/comment text, or provide a separate parsed-command field and skip inference for label target context.

**Comments:** This is separate from the regex breadth: even precise “follow-up PR” wording can be accidental when it comes from the target PR body.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: the unresolved issues are concrete branch changes and are safe for an automated fix-pr pass with focused negative tests.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items
- [ ] Narrow stacked/follow-up intent detection so ordinary “stacked” prose does not derive `base_pr`, and add false-positive tests.
- [ ] Guard base derivation so it only runs on explicit user command/comment text, not PR title/body context from label-triggered implement runs.
